subject: How to calculate test information statistics for three groups

messages.author: c3edf00917ec6491
messages.subject: How to calculate test information statistics for three groups
parts:
Hi Phil,

I have generated graphs for item and test information functions, with TIFs comparing groups (with two groups compared on each of three plots), for total and (four) factor scores. My question is, is there a code for generating the test information statistic itself (preferably across degrees of theta, -3 to +3), rather than needing to approximate it from a plot?

Thanks,
Seb

messages.subject: Re: How to calculate test information statistics for three groups
parts:
group is the name of an individual value in your grouping variable? This input should be a character like group = 'group1', group = 'reference', or something to that degree, indicating the literal grouping subset to pull out the single-group information. Also, some reproducible code would be helpful to track down the problem quicker.

Phil

parts:
Hi again,

I got it to work using the code below:

# Remove age column
newdat <- dat [,2:21]

# Make age into a separate vector
group <- c(rep('Early', sum(dat$age == "Age 18-30")),
           rep('Middle', sum(dat$age == "Age 31-49")),
           rep('Late', sum(dat$age == "Age 50+")))

# Specify theta, run multiplegroup 
Theta <- matrix(seq(-6,6,.1))
mg <- multipleGroup(newdat, mirt.model('F1 = 1-20'), group)

# generate testinfo
tI <- map_dfr(1:3, ~{
  groups <- c("Early", 'Middle', "Late")
  ti <- testinfo(mg, Theta, group = .x)
  data.frame(information = ti, xAxis = Theta, se = 1/(sqrt(ti)), group = groups[.x], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})

## print testinfo
print(tI)

Thanks again for your help.
